title: Szczecin Day Trip from Berlin - Quick Summary
items: **The direct Berlin to Szczecin train is not running until 12 December 2026.** The line is being rebuilt, so every trip is RE3 to Angermünde plus the RB66 replacement bus, or a longer all rail detour via Pasewalk. Times checked on 3 September 2026.

**Fastest pattern: about 2 hours 22 minutes.** RE3 from Berlin Gesundbrunnen at 08:32, RE30 and RE4 via Pasewalk, into Szczecin Główny at 10:54. The bus bridge route takes about 3 hours, or about 2 and a half with the express bus that runs on the alternate hours.

**The right ticket for most visitors is the VBB 24 hour ticket Berlin AB to Szczecin at 33.60 euros.** It covers the whole corridor via Tantow plus Szczecin trams and buses all day. A single is 16.80 euros. The Deutschlandticket ends at the border; the add on from Tantow is 4.40 euros one way or 8.80 for a 24 hour ticket.
**Groups of up to 5 should use the Brandenburg-Berlin-Ticket**, valid to Szczecin on weekdays from 09:00 and all day on weekends, including Szczecin city transport.

**On the ground, everything worth a first visit is walkable from the station**: the 12:00 Underground Routes shelter tour at Kolumba 2, the rebuilt Old Town, the castle courtyard, the Wały Chrobrego terrace, the prize winning Philharmonic and a pasztecik at the 1969 bar on Wojska Polskiego.
**Carry your passport or ID card.** Germany runs temporary checks at its land borders, so spot checks on the bus or train are possible in both directions.
